summary: Count to 100 by ones and tens from any number; count back from 10 and from 20.
Read, write, and show numbers 0 to 20 with numerals, objects, or pictures.
Link counting to quantity: one number per object, last number tells how many, each next is one more.
Tell how many by subitizing up to 5 or counting up to 20 objects; count out a given amount.
Compare two groups of up to 20 objects using words like more, fewer, same.
Compare written numbers up to 20 using comparison words.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently, with the equal sign on either side.
Build and break apart 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones; record it.
Show adding and subtracting within 10 with objects, fingers, drawings, acting out, or equations.
Solve add and subtract story problems within 10 with objects or drawings and explain.
Split numbers up to 10 into two parts in different ways and record each split.
Find the number that goes with 1 to 9 to make 10.
Name shapes around you and describe where things are: above, below, beside, behind.
Name shapes in any size or turn; tell which pictures are or are not the shape.
Sort shapes into flat and solid; see flat faces on solid shapes.
Compare flat and solid shapes by sides, corners, and other features using everyday words.
Build shapes from materials like sticks and clay and draw shapes.
Put simple shapes together to make bigger shapes.
Name things you can measure about objects, such as length or weight.
Compare two objects directly to see which has more or less of something.
Sort objects into two groups (up to 20 each), count each group, and order by count.
Name pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters and their values; trade coins equal to a dime.
Connect counting on and back to adding and subtracting.
Add and subtract within 20 with mental strategies; be fluent within 10.
Find 1 more, 1 less, 10 more, 10 less than a two-digit number in your head.
Count to 120 forward and back by ones, fives, and tens; read and write these numbers.
Know a two-digit number is tens and ones; write it in several forms.
Solve add and subtract story problems within 20 with the unknown anywhere.
Solve story problems adding three numbers with a total up to 20.
Use properties like order and grouping to add and subtract.
Think of subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Know the equal sign means same value; decide if equations are true or false.
Find the missing number in an add or subtract equation with three numbers.
Compare two two-digit numbers by tens and ones using >, =, <.
Add within 99, including two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten, using models and place value.
Subtract multiples of ten from multiples of ten using models and place-value strategies.
Tell defining from non-defining shape features; build and draw shapes with given features.
Combine flat or solid shapes into new shapes and make more shapes from them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more pieces means smaller pieces.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length by lining up same-size units end to end with no gaps.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Use tallies and tables for up to 3 categories; make bar and picture graphs and answer questions.
Find the value of a group of one kind of coin, up to 50 cents.
Add and subtract within 20 mentally; know all one-digit sums by memory.
Know a three-digit number is hundreds, tens, and ones; 100 is ten tens.
Count forward and back within 1000; skip-count by 2s, 5s, 10s, and 100s.
Read and write numbers to 1000 in standard, word, unit, and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers by place value using >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place-value and property strategies.
Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.
Add or subtract 10 or 100 mentally from a number between 100 and 900.
Explain in writing or drawings why add and subtract strategies work.
Solve one- and two-step add and subtract story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 1000 with models and place value, regrouping when needed.
Tell if up to 20 objects is odd or even; write evens as doubles.
Find totals in arrays up to 5 by 5 with repeated addition equations.
Recognize and draw shapes with given angles or faces; name triangles to hexagons and cubes.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds, fourths and describe the whole.
Measure length with rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, or tapes.
Measure one object with two units and explain how the results relate.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another.
Solve length story problems within 100 with drawings and equations.
Make a number line and show whole numbers, sums, and differences up to 100 on it.
Tell time to 5 minutes with a.m. and p.m.; use half past and quarter after.
Solve money problems with bills and coins using $ and cent signs.
Measure lengths and show the data on a whole-number line plot.
Draw picture and bar graphs for up to four categories and solve problems with them.
Understand unit and other fractions as equal parts of a whole or set; model them and solve problems.
Place fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal parts.
Find equivalent fractions, write wholes as fractions, and compare same-numerator or same-denominator fractions.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know one-digit products by memory.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 and use estimates in problems.
Add and subtract within 1000 fluently with strategies and algorithms.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 such as 9 x 80.
Interpret a product as a number of equal groups.
Interpret a quotient as sharing or grouping equally.
Solve multiply and divide story problems within 100 with drawings and equations.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use properties of operations to multiply and divide.
See division as finding a missing factor.
Solve two-step story problems with equations and check answers by estimating.
Find, make, and extend number patterns and explain them.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000 using >, =, <.
Shapes can share features that define bigger groups, like quadrilaterals.
Split shapes into equal-area parts and name each as a unit fraction.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in grams, kilograms, liters; solve one-step problems.
Draw scaled picture and bar graphs and answer how-many-more questions.
Measure lengths to half and quarter inches and show data on a line plot.
Understand area as square units that cover a shape with no gaps.
Find area by counting unit squares.
Link area to multiplying side lengths and to the distributive property; combined rectangles moved to grade 4.
Solve perimeter problems, including missing sides and same perimeter with different areas.
Tell time to the minute, find elapsed time (also over an hour), and solve time problems.
Solve two-step money problems with coins and bills over a dollar using $ and cent signs.
Each place is worth ten times the place to its right, up to 1,000,000.
Read, write, compare, and order whole numbers up to 1,000,000.
Round whole numbers to any place and estimate with compatible numbers.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers with a standard algorithm.
Multiply up to 4 digits by 1 digit and 2 digits by 2 digits; explain with models.
Divide up to 4-digit numbers by 1 digit, with remainders; explain with models.
Explain equivalent fractions with models and generate them.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using common parts or benchmarks.
See fractions as sums of unit fractions; decompose them and check sums with benchmarks.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including story problems.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number and solve related story problems.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths to add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals.
Compare decimals to hundredths and justify with models.
Read a multiplication equation as a comparison like 3 times as many.
Solve multiplicative comparison story problems with drawings and equations.
Solve multi-step whole-number story problems, interpret remainders, and check by estimating.
Find factor pairs and multiples to 100 and tell prime from composite.
Make and extend number or shape patterns from a rule and notice features.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Sort shapes by parallel or perpendicular sides and angle types; identify right triangles.
Find and draw lines of symmetry.
Know relative sizes of units in one system and convert larger units to smaller.
Solve multi-step measurement problems with whole numbers and simple fractions; no decimals.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real problems.
Make line plots with halves, fourths, eighths and solve problems from them.
Understand angles and that they are measured in degrees as parts of a circle.
Measure angles in whole degrees with a protractor.
Angle measures add; find unknown angles with equations.
Find areas of shapes made of rectangles by splitting them and adding or subtracting.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators using equivalents.
Solve fraction add and subtract story problems and check with benchmark fractions.
See a fraction as division and solve sharing problems with fraction answers.
Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction and explain with models and stories.
Treat multiplying as scaling and predict product size without computing.
Solve real problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
A digit is worth ten times the place to its right and a tenth of the left place.
Explain patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use exponents.
Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths in several forms.
Round decimals to any place and estimate answers.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers with a standard algorithm.
Divide up to 4-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers and explain with models.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths and justify the method.
Evaluate expressions with grouping symbols and compare two simple expressions.
Write simple expressions and interpret them without computing.
Make two patterns from two rules, compare terms, and graph the pairs.
Understand coordinate axes, origin, and ordered pairs.
Graph points in the first quadrant to solve problems and interpret them.
Features of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Sort quadrilaterals into a hierarchy by properties and justify in writing.
Convert units within one system and use them in multi-step problems.
Make line plots with fractions of a unit and solve problems from them.
Understand volume as unit cubes filling a solid with no gaps.
Find volume by counting unit cubes.
Find volume of boxes with formulas and by adding two boxes.
Find areas of rectangles with fraction sides by tiling and by multiplying.

state_code: # STATUS: FINAL. Revised K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Mathematics ("2025 LSSM", new Bulletin 142).
# - BESE approved March 2026; final rule repealing and re-promulgating Bulletin 142 published in the Louisiana Register, LR 52:1128-1137 (July 2026).
# - Required from 2027-28: LDOE FAQ (updated April 15, 2026) says full implementation is 2027-2028; 2026-27 is a learning year
#   (keep teaching the 2016 standards); the spring 2027 LEAP still tests the 2016 standards.
# - 2025 Louisiana Student Standards for Mathematics (LDOE, gives the codes):
# - K-12 LSSM Crosswalk (official, 2016 code -> 2025 code, with strike/underline edits); used for every ccss mapping:
# - LAC Title 28 Part CXLII, Bulletin 142 as promulgated (legal text, no codes): https://doa.la.gov/media/noxomnvm/28v142.docx
# - Grade K-5 Standards Resource Guides (Aug 2026), e.g. https://doe.louisiana.gov/docs/default-source/academic-standards/grade-4-standards-resource-guide.pdf
# - The 2016 LSSM kept CCSS codes for all CCSS content, so the crosswalk's 2016 codes are CCSS codes, except LA-only
# - Grade.Domain.Cluster.Number, e.g. 3.NOF.A.1, 4.DM.D.8. Numbers run on through a grade's domain (K.NOF.A.1 ... K.NOF.E.8), not per cluster.
#   The standards PDF prints cluster codes, e.g. "(K.NOF.B)", and numbers; the crosswalk and resource guides write full codes.
# - Lettered parts (a, b, c) and bullets are folded into their standard. Each grade also lists "Grade Level (Expected) Foundational Skills"
#   (numbered 1-8, no codes); these restate standards and are not rows. Standards for Math Practice (8, K-12) skipped.
# DOMAINS (K-5, same four in every grade)
# - NOF Numeracy and Operational Fluency; AR Algebraic Reasoning; GL Geometric Reasoning and Logic; DM Data Analysis and Measurement.
# - CCSS domains are regrouped: CC, NBT, NF and fluency standards mostly go to NOF; OA and some NBT computation to AR; G to GL; MD to DM.
# - None. Every CCSS K-5 standard appears in the crosswalk with a 2025 code.
# - Partly: 3.MD.C.7d (area of rectilinear figures) stays in grade 4 (4.DM.D.8), as in 2016; 4.MD.A.2 problems omit decimals;
#   5.G.B.4 classifies only quadrilaterals; 5.NF.B.4b (area with fractional sides) split off to 5.DM.D.6; 4.NF.B.3c-d split off to 4.NOF.D.10.
# - Money: K.DM.C.4 (coin names, values, trades within a dime), 1.DM.D.5 (one coin type up to 50 cents), 3.DM.E.9 (two-step problems with bills over $1).
# - Grade 3 compares and orders whole numbers to 100,000 (3.AR.D.9, new in 2025; CCSS compares multi-digit numbers in 4.NBT.A.2).
# - Subitizing in K (K.NOF.B.4); counting back from 10 and 20 in K; counting by 5s and backward in grade 1; skip-counting by 2s in grade 2.
# - K comparisons extended from 10 to 20; grade 1 makes bar and picture graphs (CCSS 2.MD.D.10); elapsed time over 60 minutes in grade 3;
#   comparing simple expressions in grade 5 (5.AR.A.1a); estimation with compatible numbers (4.NOF.A.3, 5.NOF.C.11).
# - Two code layouts exist for grades 4-5. The LDOE standards PDF, crosswalk and resource-guide headings use the codes here. The legal LAC text
#   (and the BESE comparison doc) has no codes and groups grade 4-5 clusters differently (e.g. grade 4 NOF: A fractions, ..., E place value,
#   F add/subtract; grade 4 AR adds C compare whole numbers, D multiply/divide; grade 5 AR adds C powers of ten/decimals, D divide/decimal ops).
#   Some achievement-level tables inside the Aug 2026 resource guides use codes that fit that LAC layout (4.AR.D.6, 5.AR.C.4, 5.NOF.D.10).
#   Codes for grades 4-5 NOF/AR may be renumbered later; K-3 layouts agree.
# - Minor wording differs between the LDOE PDF and the LAC text (e.g. 1.AR.E.8 "Add up to 99" in the LAC); content mapping is unaffected.
# - 3.AR.D.9 is "n/a" (new) in the crosswalk; marked moved from 4.NBT.A.2 here. Money rows marked moved from 2.MD.C.8 (CCSS has money only there).
# - 1.DM.C.4 lists 2.MD.D.10 too because it adds making bar and picture graphs.
# - same vs edited is a judgement on content; added examples, "real-world tasks" wording, written explanations, and sub-part splits count as same.
